3G-RNC|M1000C72.Description:
This counter, divided by the denominator counter, indicates the average code usage in percentage in a measurement period.
Average code usage is calculated as the ratio between the number of unavailable SFx codes and the number of all (available and unavailable) SFx codes, where SFx refers to the highest spreading factor. Note that the SFx codes may be unavailable due to two reasons: the code is allocated, or the code is unavailable because another code is allocated in the same code tree branch and thus prevents the use of the SFx code.

3G-RNC|M1000C138.Description:
The ratio of transmitted non-HSPA power and the maximum transmission power possible to use on that DL carrier at that moment. 
If only HSDPA is enabled, the non-HSPA power is the transmitted carrier power of all codes not used for HS-PDSCH or HS-SCCH transmission. If HSUPA is enabled, the non-HSPA power is the transmitted carrier power of all codes not used for HS-PDSCH, HS-SCCH, E-AGCH, E-RGCH or E-HICH transmission.

3G-RNC|M1000C138.Updated:
This counter is updated periodically according to the RNC internal timer whose period is defined by parameter WBTS->RRIndPeriod. When the timer expires, the latest received non-HSPA power value in NBAP:PRIVATE:RADIO RESOURCE MEASUREMENT REPORT is used for counter update.
This counter is updated even if there are not any HS-DSCH allocations in the cell.

3G-RNC|M1000C176.Description: The number of acknowledged PRACH preambles reported by the BTS indicates the RACH channel load. This counter, divided by the denominator, gives the average number of acknowledged PRACH preambles during the Radio Resource Indication period. This counter is updated only for cells using the 3GPP Iub interface. However due to 3GPP NBAP protocol reporting range, the counter remains mostly zero in live network environment and thus does not give useful information about the RACH load.

3G-RNC|M1000C178.Updated:

3G-RNC|M1000C396.Description:
The maximum amount of spreading codes that would be possible to allocate for Rel99 downlink users. The amount of codes is represented by SF256 level so for example one SF128 code contributes to the counter by value 2, and one SF64 code by value 4.
This counter is used when calculating a KPI about the Rel99 DL code utilization per operator. The counter is relevant only if feature "RAN2412 Inter Circle Roaming" is enabled. The value remains zero if the feature is disabled.

The amount of codes is calculated as: 
Total number of SF256 codes in the code tree) - (Reserved SF256 codes)

Where:
Total number of SF256 codes in the code tree = 256
Reserved SF256 codes = Sum of all the codes used by common channels, HSPA control channels, minimum number of HS-PDSCH codes, F-DPCH codes, codes used by Iur users and codes used by SRB on DCH for which IMSI is not known.
Minimum number of HS-PDSCH codes is lowest value in the HSPDSCHCodeSet parameter.

3G-RNC|M1000C398.Description: The number of total uplink power (RTWP) measurement report samples in which the power value is less than -110 dBm. This counter can be used to detect possible antenna line failures.

3G-RNC|M1000C398.Updated: This counter is updated periodically according to the RNC internal timer whose period with WBTS is RRIndPeriod and with NBxxx the period is min(PrxTotalReportPeriod, PtxTotalPeriod). 3G-RNC|M1000C406.Description:
The duration of Mass Event Handler load state being active in a cell. 
This state means that the length of NRT scheduling queue has exceeded a threshold defined by WCEL-MEHQueueThreshold and WCEL-MEHLoadStateTtT. In this state, longer Traffic Volume Pending time, temporary maximum bitrate for UL DCH, and temporarily limited maximum number of HSUPA users may be active depending on what functions are enabled with parameter WCEL-MassEventHandler.

The impact of MEH activation can be checked with M1006C301, M1002C685 and M1002C686.

When the RNC receives an RANAP: IU RELEASE COMMAND from the CN, and the RNC has not sent an RANAP: IU RELEASE REQUEST message to the CN before that, and no other Iu connections for the UE exist.

Exception 1: This counter is updated if the RRC connection is released due to PS inactivity (even though RNC sends an RANAP: IU RELEASE REQUEST message to the CN in this case).

Exception 2: This counter is not updated in case of SRNS relocation, inter-RNC hard handover, or inter-system handover.

Exception 3: This counter is not updated if the RANAP: IU RELEASE COMMAND cause is "Requested Ciphering and/or Integrity Protection Algorithms not Supported". In that case counter M1001C19 is updated instead.

3G-RNC|M1001C64.Updated:
When the target-RNC receives RANAP: RELOCATION REQUEST from the core network for initiating the hard handover procedure. If however the core network later cancels the procedure, also the counter update is canceled, i.e. the counter includes only those cases where the actual handover attempt was done from UE point of view.

It is not always possible for the target RNC to distinguish whether the incoming hard handover is intra-frequency or inter-frequency and therefore this counter can sometimes be updated also in the inter-frequency inter-RNC hard handover.

When the RNC receives either an RANAP: RAB ASSIGNMENT REQUEST (release RAB) or RANAP: IU RELEASE COMMAND message from the CN, and the RNC has sent an IU/RAB RELEASE REQUEST message to the CN before that, and the release is requested due to some failure not covered by the other failure counters, and the RAB type is PS data interactive. If the CN does not send a release message to the RNC within certain time period, the RAB is released anyway and this counter is updated.

3G-RNC|M1001C223.Description:
This counter denotes the sum of RAB setup times for CS voice. This counter, divided by the denominator (see the Dependencies), gives the average RAB setup time for CS voice. The RAB setup time is defined as the time between the RANAP: RAB ASSIGNMENT REQUEST and RANAP: RAB ASSIGNMENT RESPONSE messages during RAB establishment or the time between the RANAP: RAB ASSIGNMENT REQUEST and RRC: RADIO BEARER SETUP COMPLETE (or RRC:RADIO BEARER RECONFIGURATION COMPLETE) in case Accelerated Voice Setup feature is active.

NOTE: setup time covers both the RAB Setup and RAB Access phases.

3G-RNC|M1001C237.Network Element Name: RAB ACT FAIL FOR MULTI RAB WITH AMR AND NRT
3G-RNC|M1001C237.Network Element Name in issue 05: RAB ACT FAIL FOR MULTI RAB WITH AMR AND NRT
3G-RNC|M1001C237.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: RAB ACT FAIL FOR MULTI RAB WITH AMR AND NRT
3G-RNC|M1001C237.Description: The number of RAB Active Failures for Multi-RAB with AMR and PS NRT connections. This counter is updated only if both the CS and the PS RABs drop simultaneously, which does not usually occur in live network scenarios because the CS re-establishment timer is shorter than the PS re-establishment timer. Therefore, it is recommended to monitor Multi RAB drops using counter M1001C703, which is updated when either the PS or the CS RAB drops, regardless of whether the drop is simultaneous or not.

3G-RNC|M1001C714.Description:
The number of CS Voice call RAB active failures after the UE has reported detected set cell in 1A or 1C event, and handover could not be initiated because the reported cell is not included in ADJS or ADJD list.

Also one of RAB Active Failure counters is updated along with this counter.

3G-RNC|M1001C714.Updated: When CS voice call RAB active failure happens within 10 seconds after receiving 1A/1C event from the UE asking to add non-identified detected set cell to the active set. 3G-RNC|M1001C728.Description:
The number of RRC connections established by UEs supporting DB-HSDPA band combination Rel9-1. This refers to table 5.0aA of 3GPP TS 25.101. Configuration 9-1 means UL band I (2100 MHz) or VIII (900 MHz) and DL bands I (2100 MHz) and VIII (900 MHz).
It is possible that also M1001C729 and M1001C730 are updated along with this counter if the UE supports multiple DB-HSDPA band combinations.

3G-RNC|M1002C475.Network Element Name: DCH SELECTED FOR INTERACTIVE DUE TO MAX HSDPA USERS
3G-RNC|M1002C475.Network Element Name in issue 05: DCH SELECTED FOR INTERACTIVE DUE TO MAX HSDPA USERS
3G-RNC|M1002C475.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: DCH SELECTED FOR INTERACTIVE DUE TO MAX HSDPA USERS
3G-RNC|M1002C475.Description:
The number of times when the DCH channel type is selected for interactive class connections due to maximum amount of HSDPA users or MAC-d flows in the WBTS, local cell group or cell.
The counter includes also HS-DSCH rejections due to temporary HSDPA user amount restriction applied by feature RAN2954.
On SRNC the counter is updated only in the initial user plane allocations, it is not updated if DCH x/y to HSDPA switch or serving cell change fails due to the maximum number of users reached. On DRNC the counter is updated also in channel type switch and serving cell change failures.

The number of successful E-DCH resource allocations for Signalling Radio Bearer in the DRNC. The downlink SRB channel type is Rel99 DCH. The E-DCH transport channel is configured with 2 ms TTI when SRBs are mapped on E-DCH/DCH. 
Note that successful E-DCH resource allocation does not yet mean that the allocation would be successful from end user point of view.

3G-RNC|M1002C685.Network Element Name: MASS EVENT HANDLER RESTRICTED R99 UL BITRATE
3G-RNC|M1002C685.Network Element Name in issue 05: MASS EVENT HANDLER RESTRICTED R99 UL BITRATE
3G-RNC|M1002C685.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: MASS EVENT HANDLER RESTRICTED R99 UL BITRATE
3G-RNC|M1002C685.Description:
The number of Rel99 UL DCH bitrate selections where the bitrate is restricted due to temporary maximum bitrate of Mass Event Handler feature being active. The restriction is triggered because the NRT scheduling queue length exceeded the threshold defined by WCEL-MEHQueueThreshold and WCEL-MEHLoadStateTtT.
Additionally, restriction can be triggered when the RAN3266 EMEH feature is configured to limit UL NRT bitrate allocation in a cell when Preventive or Reactive EMEH cell state is active. In this case, the temporary bitrate limitation is set to initial bitrate level. Counter update triggers only when the EMEH bitrate limitation solely prevents a bitrate allocation, that is higher than initial bitrate for the UL DCH.

The number of times when the RNC admission control entity rejected a request due to BTS signaling load reason. The rejected request can be PS user plane allocation or NRT RAB setup.

Along with this counter, other M1001, M1002, and M1022 failure counters can also be updated indicating setup failure due to BTS. This counter only provides additional information on top of the existing counters.

3G-RNC|M1002C736.Description: This counter denotes the time that UEs are in Cell_DCH state without userplane resources for RABs. This counter is updated with the time that a UE is in CELL_DCH state without any user plane resources for RABs (UE with SRBs-only configuration) until a UE gets user plane resources for any RAB, or the situation of the UE changes so that it does not need the user plane resources. When divided by the denominator, this counter gives the average time that one UE is in Cell_DCH state without user plane resources. The update is done in all active set cells of UEs.

3G-RNC|M1006C86.Network Element Name in issue 05: STATE TRANS CELL_DCH TO CELL_FACH DUE TO LOW UTILISATION
3G-RNC|M1006C86.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: STATE TRANS CELL_DCH TO CELL_FACH DUE TO LOW UTILISATION
3G-RNC|M1006C86.Description:
The number of RRC state transitions from CELL_DCH state to CELL_FACH or PCH state due to low DCH utilisation. If downlink or uplink throughput in the number of bytes goes below the threshold defined with the RNC configuration parameters DCHutilRelThrDL or DCHutilRelThrUL, the PS DCH release procedure starts.
This counter can be updated both for Rel99 DCH/DCH and HSDPA. For HSDPA calls the counter is updated if the final trigger to initiate state transition was uplink low utilization. But if the final trigger was HS-DSCH downlink low utilization, the counter is not updated even if before that also uplink low utilization indication would have been received from L2.

3G-RNC|M1006C170.Description:
Sum of state transition times from Cell-PCH or URA-PCH state to Cell-FACH state, defined as the time between: RRC: Cell Update (cause: UL Data Transmission or Paging response) - RRC: positive UL-DCCH ack as a response to Cell Update Confirm.
This counter, divided by the denominator, provides the average state transition time.
When the UE is/was in PCH state with RNTIs allocated and transfers itself to HS-FACH state by sending ("dummy") RRC: Measurement Report, the counter is updated by value zero because the state transition is completed immediately when the RNC receives the Measurement Report.

3G-RNC|M1006C251.Description: The number of low priority paging records that were dropped in L2 scheduling.
3G-RNC|M1006C251.Description in issue 05: The number of low priority paging records that were dropped in L2 scheduling.
3G-RNC|M1006C251.Description in release FP22R1: The number of low priority paging records that were dropped in L2 scheduling.
3G-RNC|M1006C251.Updated:
RNC L2 drops low priority paging message because of following scenarios.
a) Paging congestion on SFN:
Paging record needs to be scheduled on a SFN as per its paging occasion. Multiple high/low priority paging records and high priority messages like ETWS/BCCH, can map to the same SFN on a paging transport channel. Due to Transport Block size limitation low  priority paging records are dropped on that SFN.
b) SFN jump:
 Paging transport channel's SFN alignment can happen per UL SYNCRONIZATION/TIMING ADJUSTMENT FP frame. This could result in skipping of some SFNs when there is a forward correction of SFN at RNC. Paging records in the skipped SFNs are dropped.
c) Transport block memory allocation failure:
If a paging record cannot be stored in RNC L2 during scheduling because of memory allocation failure then that paging record is dropped.

"Establishment cause" is an optional IE in the Cell Update message introduced by 3GPP Rel5.

Also one of basic Cell Update counters M1006C34-M1006C40 is updated along with this counter depending on the "Cell update cause" IE used by the UE.

3G-RNC|M1006C255.Description:
The number of RRC connection sessions in which a UE has been identified as a Rel5 Legacy Fast Dormancy phone (LFDphone) based on the "Signalling Connection Release Indication (SCRI) without cause" from the UE.
This UE is able to easily send SCRIwithoutCause in the future and by RAN2451 feature, RNC tries to avoid idle state and uses Cell_PCH instead.
This means that for RRC connection sessions during which:
- RNC has identified UE as a Rel5-iPhone and after every SCRIwithoutCause, RNC will move UE to Cell_PCH instead of idle or
- RNC has identified UE as a Rel5-non-iPhone (which IMSI had been stored after previous SCRI for some time) and during this session, the RNC uses Smart timers in order to avoid idle state.

3G-RNC|M1006C256.Network Element Name: LFDPHONE FACH OR DCH TO PCH SUCCESS

3G-RNC|M1006C256.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: LFDPHONE FACH OR DCH TO PCH SUCCESS
3G-RNC|M1006C256.Description:
The number of times when a Rel5 Legacy Fast Dormancy phone (LFDphone) has made a successful transition to Cell/URA_PCH state.
This means that for cases (after SCRIwithoutCause during the current or the previous session) when:
- RNC moves Rel5-iPhone to Cell_PCH immediately after SCRIwithoutCause and later moves it again due to SCRI or due to RNC timer (NOTE: iPhone still uses normal inactivity timers).
- RNC moves Rel5-non-iPhone to Cell_PCH before SCRIwithoutCause (after using Smart timers in this session due to stored IMSI after SCRIwithoutCause in the previous session).
Also, other state transition counters (for example M1006C47, M1006C49 or M1006C114) are updated along with this counter.

This number includes also cases when the increased Traffic Volume Measurement pending time was used because of temporary HSDPA user amount restriction due to Voice Call Priorization During High Traffic Load. Additionally, increased Traffic Volume Measurement pending time usage triggers when the RAN3266 EMEH feature is configured to activate the functionality in EMEH cell states.

This means state transitions where the UE did not set "Traffic volume indicator" flag in the Cell Update message, but the RNC still chooses Cell_DCH as the target state based on the previous data transfer activity of the UE.

Also the generic PCH to DCH state transition counters are updated along with this counter.

3G-RNC|M1007C36.Description:
This counter is updated, when UE sends a periodic measurement report triggered
by event 1B to the RNC in order to remove a cell from the active set. That situation can appear, for example, when the RNC is prevented to delete the old branch to the active set before the new branch is synchronised. Event 1B triggered periodic reporting is controlled with the Drop Window and Drop Reporting Interval parameters.

Only the serving RNC (SRNC) can update the counter. The counter is updated in
every cell that is in the active set on the SRNC side when the RNC receives
the measurement report.

3G-RNC|M1008C17.Description: The number of connection drops on SRNC side during intra-frequency hard handover procedure. --- If neither the target RNC has received the handover complete message nor the source RNC has received a failure message from the UE, the source and target RNCs may delete both old and new configurations. Note that if RRC connection re-establishment is enabled, this failure situation does not always mean the drop of RRC connection but only the loss of Cell_DCH state radio connection.

3G-RNC|M1008C321.Updated:
After the handover, the control entity has made a handover decision. In inter-RNC case, the RNC sends an RANAP: RELOCATION REQUIRED message to the CN. In intra-RNC case, the RNC sends an RRC: PHYSICAL CHANNEL RECONFIGURATION, TRANSPORT CHANNEL

3G-RNC|M1010C13.Description in release FP22R1: This counter indicates the number of times when an inter-system HHO measurement ends due to uplink DCH quality without making an inter-system HHO attempt, because no cell is good enough for inter-system HHO - for UEs with RT connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C13.Updated: The counter is updated when the handover control entity decides that there is no suitable GSM target cell in terms of RX level, or the target GSM cell is suitable, but its BSIC verification fails - after the maximum number of periodical inter-RAT (GSM) measurement reports (more information can be found in the Handover control document). If the UE fails to establish the physical channel(s) indicated in the handover command, the UE will revert to the configuration prior to the reception of the handover command (old configuration) and transmit a failure message to the source RNC. The hard handover procedure ends and the UE resumes the normal operation as if no hard handover attempt had occurred.

3G-RNC|M1010C217.Description:
The number of unsuccessful inter-system handovers caused by Directed Retry for AMR calls. If the UE fails to establish the physical channel(s) indicated in the handover command, the UE will revert to the configuration prior to the reception of the handover command (old configuration) and transmit a failure message to the source RNC.
From end user point of view a failure in Directed Retry triggered ISHO means a failed CS Voice call attempt.

3G-RNC|M1010C239.Description:
The total duration for LTE frequency band measurements in SRNC. The start time of the measurement is when the Measurement Control is sent to the UE. 
The stop trigger for the measurement is when the measurement session ends either to perform the redirection/handover or not because no suitable carrier is found or the call was released or dropped during the measurement.

The counter is updated only for the main cell of the connection.

3G-RNC|M1010C309.Description: This counter denotes the number of decisions for inter-system HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM after measuring with or without compressed mode due to bad C/I ratio for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C309.Description in issue 05: This counter denotes the number of decisions for inter-system HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM after measuring with or without compressed mode due to bad C/I ratio for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C309.Description in release FP22R1: This counter denotes the number of decisions for inter-system HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM after measuring with or without compressed mode due to bad C/I ratio for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C309.Updated: This counter is updated when either the handover control entity decides to make an inter-system HHO attempt or the handover control entity decides that no cell is good enough for handover after inter-system measurements with or without compressed mode. This counter is updated only when the trigger reason for inter-system HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM is bad C/I ratio. This counter is not updated if the call is released during the measurement or the UE does not send measurement reports as expected.

This counter is not updated if the call is released during the measurement or the UE does not send measurement reports as expected.

3G-RNC|M1010C310.Description: This counter denotes the number of times when an inter-system measurement for HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM due to bad C/I ratio ends without making an inter-system HHO attempt to GSM, because no cell is good enough for inter-system HHO - for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C310.Description in issue 05: This counter denotes the number of times when an inter-system measurement for HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM due to bad C/I ratio ends without making an inter-system HHO attempt to GSM, because no cell is good enough for inter-system HHO - for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.
3G-RNC|M1010C310.Description in release FP22R1: This counter denotes the number of times when an inter-system measurement for HHO from WCDMA-LTE border area to GSM due to bad C/I ratio ends without making an inter-system HHO attempt to GSM, because no cell is good enough for inter-system HHO - for UEs with CS and/or PS connection.

3G-RNC|M1013C0.Network Element Name: NUMBER OF INTRA FREQUENCY SHO ATTEMPTS
3G-RNC|M1013C0.Network Element Name in issue 05: NUMBER OF INTRA FREQUENCY SHO ATTEMPTS
3G-RNC|M1013C0.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: NUMBER OF INTRA FREQUENCY SHO ATTEMPTS
3G-RNC|M1013C0.Description:
The number of intra-frequency soft handover attempts. Inter-RNC soft handover and the inter-RNC intra-frequency hard handover attempts are counted as well. This counter is updated for a measurement object in which source and target cells are defined. 
Branch addition and inter-RNC intra-frequency HHO: If cells A and B are in the active set and branch addition for cell C is attempted, this counter is updated by 1 for objects (A,C) and (B,C).
Branch replacement: If cells A and B are in the active set and cell B is attempted to be replaced with cell C, this counter is updated by 1 for object (A,C). 
Branch deletion: This counter is not updated in branch deletion.
3G-RNC|M1013C0.Description in issue 05:
The number of intra-frequency soft handover attempts. Inter-RNC soft handover and the inter-RNC intra-frequency hard handover attempts are counted as well. This counter is updated for a measurement object in which source and target cells are defined. 
Branch addition and inter-RNC intra-frequency HHO: If cells A and B are in the active set and branch addition for cell C is attempted, this counter is updated by 1 for objects (A,C) and (B,C).
Branch replacement: If cells A and B are in the active set and cell B is attempted to be replaced with cell C, this counter is updated by 1 for object (A,C). 
Branch deletion: This counter is not updated in branch deletion.
3G-RNC|M1013C0.Description in release FP22R1:
The number of intra-frequency soft handover attempts. Inter-RNC soft handover and the inter-RNC intra-frequency hard handover attempts are counted as well. This counter is updated for a measurement object in which source and target cells are defined. 
Branch addition and inter-RNC intra-frequency HHO: If cells A and B are in the active set and branch addition for cell C is attempted, this counter is updated by 1 for objects (A,C) and (B,C).
Branch replacement: If cells A and B are in the active set and cell B is attempted to be replaced with cell C, this counter is updated by 1 for object (A,C).

Branch replacement: If cells A and B are in the active set and cell B is attempted to be replaced with cell C, this counter is updated by 1 for object (A,C). 
Branch deletion: This counter is not updated in branch deletion.

3G-RNC|M1013C2.Description:
The sum of CPICH Ec/No difference values between source and target-cells of the handover. This counter, along with the denominator M1013C3, is used to calculate the filtered average Ec/No difference between a cell pair (source and target cells in the adjacency list) as measured by the UEs.

To convert the calculated average value into real dB difference, the following formula can be used:
CPICH_Ec/No_dB = Reported_average*0.5-24.5.

If the UE is in soft handover when the measurement report is received, the counter is updated separately for each cell in the active set, i.e. they are all considered as source-cells.

3G-RNC|M1013C8.Description:
This is the weight of soft handover cell pairs in Inter-Cell Interference Coordination (ICIC).

The counter indicates the portion of soft handovers a given cell pair takes up among all the cell pairs of ICIC data. The value is calculated by averaging the gathered data over the data gathering period.

The value placed on this counter is rounded to the nearest integer number, so it has some rounding error. This may be visible when weights of the neighbors of one cell are summed up (the sum can be something other than 100%).

The value indicates the weight of cell pair among the most used soft handover cells (top 10).  This means that soft handover cells that do not fall under the most used soft handover cells do not affect the value of this counter.

If the target cell is identified with only a cell ID and no RNC, MCC, and MNC IDs are given, then the counter falls under a use case where the target is a DRNC cell.

3G-RNC|M1017C12.Network Element Name: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU
3G-RNC|M1017C12.Network Element Name in issue 05: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU
3G-RNC|M1017C12.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU
3G-RNC|M1017C12.Description:
The average downlink PDU gross throughput of the RLC AM connection. Includes also retransmissions. Does not include periods when the DL transmission buffers in the RLC entity are empty.

The throughput calculation is done so that the used downlink active data transmission time is observed with 240 millisecond sampling periods, and if during such sampling period the sent downlink data volume exceeds 3000 bytes, the entire 240 ms period is summed to the total transfer time counter. This 240 ms value is used even if actually the RLC buffer would not have contained data all the time during the entire sampling interval.

If the transferred data volume is smaller than 3000 bytes, the transfer time counter is incremented by the actual time that there was data in the DL RLC buffer. Here the resolution is 10 ms. The sampling period falls into this category typically for example during small keepalive packet sending caused by smartphones.

3G-RNC|M1017C24.Description: The average transfer delay of transferred RLC AM SDUs in downlink. Transfer delay is the time difference between when the SDU is received from the upper layer (RRC or PDCP) and when the last PDU containing data from that SDU is acknowledged by the UE as successfully transferred. If an SDU is discarded due to SDU discard function, the transfer time is then the difference between the time when SDU is received from the upper layer and the time when SDU is discarded.

If an SDU is discarded due to SDU discard function, the transfer time is then the difference between the time when SDU is received from the upper layer and the time when SDU is discarded.

3G-RNC|M1017C50.Description: The number of connections with the 2 Mbit/s...4 Mbit/s downlink RLC PDU gross throughput. The range can be adjusted by parameters RCPMtputDLCl10to11Range and RCPMtputDLCl11to12Range. The unit of counter can be changed to "1000 bytes" by setting the RNC parameter RCPMtputAggregationLevel to a value of 1, then the counter shows the amount of data volume (with throughput in the specified range) that is transferred, instead of updating the counter by the number of transfer sessions.

The unit of counter can be changed to "1000 bytes" by setting the RNC parameter RCPMtputAggregationLevel to a value of 1, then the counter shows the amount of data volume (with throughput within the specified range) that is transferred, instead of updating the counter by the number of transfer sessions.

3G-RNC|M1022C73.Description: The number of "Congestion indication control frame - frame loss" messages sent to the BTS due to RNC UP internal buffer overflow.
3G-RNC|M1022C73.Description in issue 05: The number of "Congestion indication control frame - frame loss" messages sent to the BTS due to RNC UP internal buffer overflow.
3G-RNC|M1022C73.Description in release FP22R1: The number of "Congestion indication control frame - frame loss" messages sent to the BTS due to RNC UP internal buffer overflow.
3G-RNC|M1022C73.Updated:
RNC Frame Protocol entity sends a "Congestion Indication control frame - frame loss" indication message to the base station. 
If the situation is temporary, data loss may be avoided with automatic retransmission.
Case 1:  In some cases uplink data frames may get lost or distorted due to poor radio links or transport losses or similar reasons, then RNC may send this congestion control messages when RNC buffers are filled up while waiting for the missing frames. If the counter updates are increased heavily, this requires investigation from RNC or BTS. Such situations should be recovered when the connection is released and re-established.
Case 2: There is internal messaging between mac-es/is and RLC for handling UL data frames. When mac-es/is buffer has data but RLC is not ready to receive UL data frames as RLC is not yet configured to process the new data from UL, this leads to more buffering at mac-es/is. Due to this, buffer overflows and data is dropped, leading to congestion Indication control frame being sent to BTS.
This counter is updated for all cells in the UE's E-DCH active set controlled by the base station for which the Congestion Indication message was sent. The counter is not updated for E-DCH soft handover branches that are controlled by base stations whose Iub interfaces are not congested because the Congestion Indication message is not sent to them.

3G-RNC|M1022C231.Updated:
When L2 indicates inactivity to L3 which triggers user plane release to DCH 0/0, and finally the UE acknowledges the radio bearer reconfiguration. The original channel type can be HSxPA or Rel99 DCH x/y.
Using DCH 0/0 instead of PCH or FACH happens because the UE has got another RAB whose user plane cannot be released, for example CS call.

3G-RNC|M1022C262.Updated:
This counter is updated when one of the following Radio Bearer Reconfigurations is prevented due to bad CPICH RSCP measurement result of the active set cell:

- DC-HSDPA allocation
- Channel type switch from HSDPA to HSPA
- Upgrade of NRT DCH bit rate
- Reconfiguration of a fixed RLC PDU size in DL to a flexible RLC PDU size
- Rearrangement of a DPCH code during code tree optimization

After this counter has been updated, repetitive updates for this counter are prevented for the RRC connection until any of the above-mentioned radio bearer reconfigurations or a hard handover procedure has been completed successfully for the RRC connection.

3G-RNC|M1023C30.Description:
The amount of MAC-es/Mac-is PDU data transferred in the E-DCH in the uplink direction during the measurement interval for PS NRT connections for LTE capable UEs. The MAC-es/Mac-is PDU includes MAC-d PDU data and the 6 bits MAC-es/Mac-is header.

When DC-HSUPA is used, this counter measures separately the primary and secondary carrier E-DCH data volume.

The data transferred by High Speed CELL_FACH Users is excluded.

3G-RNC|M1026C12.Network Element Name: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR WCEL
3G-RNC|M1026C12.Network Element Name in issue 05: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR WCEL
3G-RNC|M1026C12.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR WCEL
3G-RNC|M1026C12.Description:
The average downlink PDU gross throughput of the RLC AM connection. Includes also retransmissions. Does not include periods when the DL transmission buffers in the RLC entity are empty.

The throughput calculation is done so that the used downlink active data transmission time is observed with 240 millisecond sampling periods, and if during such sampling period the sent downlink data volume exceeds 3000 bytes, the entire 240 ms period is summed to the total transfer time counter. This 240 ms value is used even if actually the RLC buffer would not have contained data all the time during the entire sampling interval.

If the transferred data volume is smaller than 3000 bytes, the transfer time counter is incremented by the actual time that there was data in the DL RLC buffer. Here the resolution is 10 ms. The sampling period falls into this category typically for example during small keepalive packet sending caused by smartphones.

3G-RNC|M1026C24.Description: The average transfer delay of transferred RLC AM SDUs in downlink. Transfer delay is the time difference between when the SDU is received from the upper layer (RRC or PDCP) and when the last PDU containing data from that SDU is acknowledged by the UE as successfully transferred. If an SDU is discarded due to SDU discard function, the transfer time is then the difference between the time when SDU is received from the upper layer and the time when SDU is discarded.

The range can be adjusted by parameters RCPMtputDLCl04to05Range and RCPMtputDLCl05to06Range. The unit of counter can be changed to "1000 bytes" by setting the RNC parameter RCPMtputAggregationLevel to a value of 1, then the counter shows the amount of data volume (with throughput within the specified range) that is transferred, instead of updating the counter by the number of transfer sessions.

3G-RNC|M1026C50.Description: The number of connections with the 2 Mbit/s...4 Mbit/s downlink RLC PDU gross throughput. The range can be adjusted by parameters RCPMtputDLCl10to11Range and RCPMtputDLCl11to12Range. The unit of counter can be changed to "1000 bytes" by setting the RNC parameter RCPMtputAggregationLevel to a value of 1, then the counter shows the amount of data volume (with throughput in the specified range) that is transferred, instead of updating the counter by the number of transfer sessions.

3G-RNC|M1027C12.Network Element Name: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR RNC
3G-RNC|M1027C12.Network Element Name in issue 05: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR RNC
3G-RNC|M1027C12.Network Element Name in release FP22R1: DL GROSS THROUGHPUT OF AM RLC PDU FOR RNC
3G-RNC|M1027C12.Description:
The average downlink PDU gross throughput of the RLC AM connection. Includes also retransmissions. Does not include periods when the DL transmission buffers in the RLC entity are empty.

The throughput calculation is done so that the used downlink active data transmission time is observed with 240 millisecond sampling periods, and if during such sampling period the sent downlink data volume exceeds 3000 bytes, the entire 240 ms period is summed to the total transfer time counter. This 240 ms value is used even if actually the RLC buffer would not have contained data all the time during the entire sampling interval.

If the transferred data volume is smaller than 3000 bytes, the transfer time counter is incremented by the actual time that there was data in the DL RLC buffer. Here the resolution is 10 ms. The sampling period falls into this category typically for example during small keepalive packet sending caused by smartphones.

If the transferred data volume is smaller than 3000 bytes, the transfer time counter is incremented by the actual time that there was data in the DL RLC buffer. Here the resolution is 10 ms. The sampling period falls into this category typically for example during small keepalive packet sending caused by smartphones.

3G-RNC|M1027C33.Counter Description: The total time period when the measurement was active in the RLC AM UL entity. The active time is the time between when the first RLC SDU arrives in the RLC buffer and when all the RLC PDUs of the packet call have been acknowledged. Periods when the transmission buffers are empty are excluded.

3G-RNC|M1028C0.Description:
Sum of linearized CPICH Ec/No values of the unidentified detected set cells reported by the UE. This counter, divided by the denominator M1028C1, provides the average CPICH Ec/No in range 0...49 defined in 3GPP TS 25.133.
After average calculation, the value can be converted to the dB unit using formula ((reporting_value/2)-24,5).

3G-RNC|M1034C38.Description:
The number of times when the DCH channel type is selected for interactive or background class connections due to maximum amount of HSDPA users or MAC-d flows in the WBTS, local cell group or cell.
On SRNC the counter is updated only in the initial user plane allocations and hard handovers, it is not updated if DCH x/y to HSDPA switch or serving cell change fails due to the maximum number of users reached. On DRNC the counter is updated also in channel type switch and serving cell change failures.
